:::{#thm-hazard-dens-surv}
#### Hazard equals density over survival

If $T$ is a continuous random variable with [density](#def-pdf) $f(t)$
and [survival function](#def-surv-fn) $\surv(t)$,
then for every $t$ with $\surv(t) > 0$:

$$\haz(t) = \frac{f(t)}{\surv(t)}$$

:::

::: proof

The proof uses two facts.
First, the event $\{T = t\}$ is a subset of the event $\{T \ge t\}$,
so intersecting them leaves $\{T = t\}$
(the [subset property](probability-basics.qmd#thm-prob-subset)).
Second, $\Pr(T = t) = 0$ for a continuous $T$,
so $\Pr(T \ge t) = \Pr(T > t) = \surv(t)$.

$$
\ba
\haz(t)
&\eqdef \p(T = t \mid T \ge t)
&& \text{(definition of the hazard function)} \\
&= \frac{\p(T = t,\, T \ge t)}{\Pr(T \ge t)}
&& \text{(definition of a conditional density)} \\
&= \frac{\p(T = t)}{\Pr(T \ge t)}
&& \text{(} \{T = t\} \subseteq \{T \ge t\} \text{)} \\
&= \frac{f(t)}{\Pr(T \ge t)}
&& \text{(} f \text{ is the density of } T \text{)} \\
&= \frac{f(t)}{\surv(t)}
&& \text{(} \Pr(T = t) = 0 \text{ for continuous } T \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-exp-haz}
#### Hazard function of an exponential distribution

Continuing @exm-exp-survfn,
for $t \ge 0$:

$$
\ba
\haz(t)
&= \frac{f(t)}{\surv(t)}
&& \text{(@thm-hazard-dens-surv)} \\
&= \frac{\lambda \ef{-\lambda t}}{\ef{-\lambda t}}
&& \text{(substitute the exponential density and survival function)} \\
&= \lambda
&& \text{(cancel } \ef{-\lambda t} \text{)}
\ea
$$

The exponential distribution has a constant hazard,
equal to its rate parameter;
for $t < 0$, $f(t) = 0$, so $\haz(t) = 0$.

:::
